files.title: European Grids Package: TEN-E regulation and permitting directive
files.lede: TEN-E trilogues under way, next on 17 November; the Council wants a deal in 2026.
files.status: The Commission proposed both on 10 December 2025. The Council agreed general approaches on the TEN-E regulation and the permitting directive at the Energy Council on 26 June 2026. In Parliament, ITRE adopted Niels Fuglsang's report on permitting on 2 July and Tsvetelina Penkova's report on TEN-E on 10 September, each with a mandate to negotiate, confirmed in plenary on 8 July and 16 September. TEN-E trilogues met on 13 October; Agence Europe reports the next on 17 November, with implementing or delegated acts and the sequencing of scenarios left to the final round. The European Council asked the co-legislators to agree the package in 2026.

ep.note: ITRE leads both; ENVI gives opinions. BUDG decided not to give one on TEN-E.

files.title: CO2 emission standards for new cars and vans (2035 target revision)
files.lede: EPP, S&D and Renew struck a deal on 20 October; ENVI votes in early November.
files.status: The Commission proposed on 16 December 2025 to lower the 2035 target for cars and vans from 100% to 90%, with credits for renewable fuels and low-carbon EU steel. ENVI leads in Parliament with Massimiliano Salini as rapporteur; ITRE and TRAN give opinions. On 20 October 2026 the EPP, S&D and Renew agreed a compromise: 87.5% for cars in 2035 plus up to 7.5 points for low-carbon EU steel, 80% for vans, and lower 2030 targets. The groups still have to sign it off. The Council took stock of progress in June 2026 and has no position yet.

files.title: Review of the Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR)
files.lede: Proposal expected before the end of 2026.
files.status: AFIR (Regulation 2023/1804) has to be reviewed by 31 December 2026. The Commission ran a call for evidence until 20 April 2026 and a public consultation from 11 May to 3 August 2026, and expects to adopt its proposal before the end of 2026. The review covers recharging and refuelling targets, including for trucks and hydrogen, payment and price transparency, and electricity supply at ports.

ep.note: No rapporteur until the proposal is out. TRAN was the lead committee on AFIR in 2023.

files.title: Medical devices and in vitro diagnostics: targeted revision of the MDR and IVDR
files.lede: SANT draft report out with 130+ amendments; Council still at working party level.
files.status: The Commission proposed on 16 December 2025 to simplify the MDR and IVDR, with adapted pathways for breakthrough and orphan devices, more proportionate surveillance and changes to software classification. SANT leads in Parliament with Oliver Schenk as rapporteur; his draft report of 1 July 2026 tables more than 130 amendments, including a new category of niche devices. IMCO named Anna Cavazzini to draft its opinion on 15 October. The Council's working party began the article-by-article examination on 23 March 2026; the June progress report says more work on the text is needed. There is no Council general approach yet.

files.title: European Biotech Act I: regulation and directive (health biotechnology)
files.lede: Council has its position on the directive; first Presidency compromise on the regulation in October.
files.status: The Commission proposed the European Biotech Act on 16 December 2025: a regulation covering health biotechnology from funding and clinical trials to authorisation and manufacturing, with a directive on genetically modified micro-organisms and the processing of organs. The Council agreed its position on the directive at the Health Council on 16 June 2026 and held a policy debate on the regulation; the Presidency tabled its first compromise text on the regulation to the working party on 8 and 9 October. In Parliament, SANT and ITRE share the regulation (Vytenis Andriukaitis and Wouter Beke) and ENVI and SANT share the directive (Marta Temido and Adam Jarubas). A Biotech Act II on the wider bioeconomy is in preparation.

files.title: Digital euro: establishment regulation
files.lede: Fifth trilogue on 20 October; next political round on 5 November.
files.status: The Commission proposed it in June 2023. The Council agreed its position on 19 December 2025. Parliament's ECON adopted Fernando Navarrete's report on 23 June 2026 and plenary confirmed the mandate on 9 July. Trilogues are under way: the fifth, on 20 October, covered offline payment limits, anti-money-laundering rules for small payments and the long-term operating model. Still open: data protection, exceptions to merchant acceptance, cash acceptance, the roll-out and use outside the euro area. The ECB aims for issuance from 2029 if the law passes.

files.title: Food and feed safety omnibus (Omnibus X): pesticides, residues, GMOs, feed
files.lede: Council mandates done; Parliament's joint ENVI-AGRI committee still to vote.
files.status: The Commission proposed the omnibus on 16 December 2025: a regulation amending ten acts on pesticides, residue levels, GMOs, feed and official controls, and a directive amending related directives. The Council agreed its position on the directive on 27 May 2026 and its mandate on the regulation on 30 September, and wants a provisional agreement by the end of 2026. In Parliament, a joint ENVI-AGRI committee leads with Michele Picaro (ECR, ENVI) and Herbert Dorfmann (EPP, AGRI); foodwatch criticised their draft report of 6 July for going further than the Commission on pesticide reviews.

files.title: European Research Area Act
files.lede: Commission proposal planned for 2026, not adopted yet.
files.status: The Commission plans to propose the ERA Act in 2026, brought forward from 2027 by Commissioner Ekaterina Zaharieva so it can pass in this mandate. It would add binding national commitments towards investing 3% of GDP in R&D, align EU and national research funding, and set conditions on research careers, research infrastructures and the freedom of scientific research. The consultation closed on 23 January 2026. Parliament adopted a resolution on the act on 10 March 2026, drafted by Eszter Lakos (EPP).

ep.note: No rapporteur until the proposal is out. Eszter Lakos drafted Parliament's resolution of 10 March 2026.

files.title: Military mobility regulation: moving troops and equipment across the EU
files.lede: Second trilogue on 20 October; a third in December on the crisis mechanism.
files.status: The Commission proposed it on 19 November 2025. Coreper agreed the Council mandate on 17 June 2026; SEDE and TRAN adopted Parliament's position on 23 June (co-rapporteurs Michał Szczerba and Roberts Zīle), confirmed in plenary on 8 July. Trilogues opened on 16 July; the second met in Strasbourg on 20 October. Agence Europe reports a third in December to settle the European Military Mobility Enhanced Response System (EMERS), private-sector involvement and the link with the Civil Protection Mechanism. The European Council asked for agreement by the end of 2026.

files.title: EU KIDS Act: minimum age for social media and safety by design for minors
files.lede: Proposed 17 September; Council working party on it 23 October; Parliament committee not yet decided.
files.status: The Commission proposed the EU KIDS Act on 17 September 2026 (COM(2026)681). Social-networking and video-sharing platforms would have to check that account holders are 15 or older, with safety-by-design duties for services used by minors, a compliance plan for very large platforms, and Commission and AI Office supervision with fines up to 6% of turnover. Henna Virkkunen is responsible for the file. In the Council, the Audiovisual and Media Working Party has examined it since 2 October. In Parliament, the referral to committee is still pending, so there is no rapporteur.
